executiveSummary: GM0928's 2025 identity, centre, population, 18 neighbourhoods, two BAG places, three settlement labels, five stations and two NWB-derived municipal-border links are coherent, and the complete deterministic ten-preset, six-checkpoint and eight-service contract passes. Release is nevertheless correction-required. Kerkrade is a hilly, densely built German-border municipality in the Roer catchment. Official analysis of the 29 June 2021 Eygelshoven event identifies short intense rainfall on wet soil, partially filled buffers, steep surface runoff, the Anselderbeek/Strijthagerbeek/Vlootsgraaf system, culverts and possible Worm backwater as distinct mechanisms. The generic named-major-river preset instead applies 1.210283 floodDepthM through T+72, up to 18,279 affected people-equivalent and 1,327,646.982 event-attributable deprived person-hours without selecting a Rhine/Meuse/IJssel reach or local hydraulic event. Pluvial T+24 separately applies 0.743429 floodDepthM and 11,078 affected people-equivalent without the official Eygelshoven 3Di/stress-test geometry, rainfall, sewer, buffers or current measures. Eight unrelated individual hazards reuse exactly the same complete neighbourhood order. Former coal-mining shafts, rising cross-border mine water, uplift/subsidence and mine-gas monitoring are real planning and monitoring contexts, but are not tectonic ground motion and cannot be inferred from the canonical near-zero earthquake preset. Public registers identify 20 water assets, a sampled Enexis planning area, 87 antenna sites, 15 education records, five stations and 67 transit stops, but no local acute-care point or live utility/restoration state. Two dated NDW obstruction records are observations, not a T+72 road forecast. Cross-border water, road/rail, energy, supply, mutual aid and Zuyderland Heerlen care dependencies are absent from the causal graph. Unsupported local consequence precision must be suppressed; missing, empty or out-of-time records remain Unknown/NoData, never zero, safe, open or available.

evidenceSources.publisher: Centraal Bureau voor de Statistiek / PDOK / Kadaster
evidenceSources.title: E01 — GM0928 official 2025 municipality, neighbourhood, place and settlement geography and statistics
evidenceSources.edition: CBS Wijken en buurten 2025; generated source snapshot retrieved 31 August 2026
supports: The annual CC BY 4.0 CBS/PDOK input identifies GM0928 as Kerkrade and reports 45,490 residents, density 2,076/km², 27.2% aged 65 or older and 9,891 one-person households; the generated centre [6.0555166705010715, 50.87354267264741] is inside the 2025 boundary.

Eighteen neighbourhood rows in three districts sum to 45,500 residents, ten above the municipality total (+0.022%); households sum to 23,130 and rounded age-65-plus rows to 12,390. Deterministic allocation reconciles exactly to 45,490 without rewriting the published rows.

BAG supplies Eygelshoven and Kerkrade; BRT supplies Eygelshoven and Kerkrade as woonkernen and Ham as a deelkern. BAG/PDOK place data are Public Domain Mark 1.0 and CBS/BRT are edition-based CC BY 4.0. Labels are not water catchments, mine zones, fire perimeters or service territories.

Home-value, housing/tenure, cars-per-household and several benefit fields each omit one neighbourhood; district-heating share and charging cover 0/18. Publisher null, suppression and non-applicability remain NoData, not zero. Annual residents do not measure commuters, border users, visitors, patients or event-time occupants.

evidenceSources.title: E02 — Analyse wateroverlast Eygelshoven and official stress-test scenarios
supports: The official retrospective reports that about 90 mm fell in two hours on the evening of 29 June 2021 after morning rain had already wetted soil and partly filled buffers. Eygelshoven experienced damaging overland flow, locally 50–60 cm measured water around Kleine Stegel and high velocities; the estimated historical return period was 350–400 years.

The analysis identifies flow from Groenstergracht/Gravenweg, Strijthagerbeek/Torenstraat, Anselderbeek and Veldhofstraat, plus restrictive Anselderbeek culverts under Nievelsteenstraat and an old industrial railway. It says prolonged lower-intensity rain stresses the Worm differently and can theoretically back up the Anselderbeek, although that did not occur in July 2021.

The official T=100 stress test is a homogeneous 61 mm in two hours scenario. It produces a different pattern and approximately 20 cm modelled water near Kleine Stegel. The authors warn that the adapted 3Di model omitted sewerage and overestimated some depths. These fields are official scenarios, not observations, current forecasts or guarantees of present protection.

The historical event used 1×1 km five-minute radar/ground inputs; scenario/model, rainfall source, soil/buffer initial state, sewer-included flag, CRS, resolution, uncertainty and NoData must travel with any reuse. No standard blanket machine-reuse licence or operational refresh cadence was identified in the PDF.

evidenceSources.title: E03 — Omgevingsvisie, cross-border Roer/Worm system, water measures and transport/energy context
evidenceSources.edition: Current Omgevingsvisie implementation page inspected 3 September 2026; programme horizons 2025–2050
supports: Kerkrade identifies the Worm and Anselderbeek as tributaries in the Roer catchment and says its local water system strongly depends on upstream German developments and management. Cooperation with Wasserverband Eifel-Rur is therefore material. This is cross-border catchment context, not a selected hydrograph or current control state.

The vision proposes investigation of dynamic operation at the Cranenweyer reservoir, removal of Anselderbeek/Strijthagerbeek culverts in Eygelshoven and erosion reduction on steep slopes. It also records an intended 2025–2026 regional water/climate-adaptation programme. Proposed investigation and programme status are planning evidence, not completed capacity.

The N300 Buitenring is identified as an important access route. The Drielandentrein connects via Eygelshoven Markt toward Herzogenrath/Aachen and onward within the euregion; residents, retail and energy planning cross the border. The national municipal graph contains no German node or operational border state.

The vision anticipates at least 100 small substations, at least three medium-voltage stations and Terwinselen high-voltage expansion, and discusses cross-border energy projects. Investment intent is planning context, not live capacity, outage, feeder topology or restoration. No standard redistribution licence or event-update cadence was identified.

evidenceSources.publisher: Gemeente Kerkrade / Provincie Limburg / Staatstoezicht op de Mijnen
evidenceSources.title: E04 — Post-mining effects, rising mine water, shaft remediation and monitoring
evidenceSources.edition: Municipal status stated for May 2025; current page inspected 3 September 2026
supports: Coal mining occurred around Kerkrade and Herzogenrath. After pumping stopped at Beerenbosch and Germany's Von Goerschen shaft, mine water began rising; the municipality says this can under some conditions cause uneven ground uplift and building damage.

The May 2025 status records specific completed, ongoing and planned industrial-shaft work, investigation of 55 suspected historical locations, 25 found shafts, 13 remediated shafts and development of a limited mine-gas monitoring programme. Each status is dated and location-specific, not a present incident or future failure forecast.

The municipality notes locations where shallow workings merit construction-specific attention. Mine-water rise, uplift/subsidence, cavity/shaft instability, gas and water-quality effects are distinct mechanisms from tectonic shaking and cannot be calibrated from a generic earthquake point source or a zero recent-catalogue count.

Public pages and monitoring plans provide no complete machine-readable deformation, fragility or service-impact field, blanket licence, coverage guarantee or operational cadence. Missing live values remain Unknown.

evidenceSources.title: E05 — Crisisplan 2024–2027 and draft renewed Limburg high-water response plan
evidenceSources.edition: Adopted crisis plan 2024–2027; high-water plan was consultation draft 15 July–26 August 2026
supports: The regional crisis plan explicitly covers international cooperation, long-duration crisis working, continuity and multidisciplinary roles. It provides governance context for Kerkrade's border setting, not live activation, staffing, supplies, completed action or a numerical recovery curve.

The 2026 public consultation notice separates three high-water scenarios: regional water systems such as streams/tributaries, Maas high water, and defence failure/polder effects. It describes an impact team using inundation maps, high-water messages and water pictures to support decisions.

The cited high-water document was still a consultation draft awaiting adoption after 26 August 2026. Neither it nor the crisis plan selects an Anselderbeek/Worm event, assigns Eygelshoven depth, or proves road, hospital, pump, shelter or utility status.

Plans support explicit incident, authority, decision, resource, action and validity ledgers. They are planning/governance evidence with policy/draft validity, not observations, forecasts or operator restoration commitments; no standard machine-reuse licence was found.

evidenceSources.publisher: Rijkswaterstaat / ProRail / OVapi / NDW / Zuyderland / RIVM
evidenceSources.title: E06 — Dutch road/rail/transit context, dated road observations and cross-boundary acute care
evidenceSources.edition: NWB-Light 1 August 2026; ProRail/GTFS/NDW snapshots retrieved 2–3 September 2026; RIVM acute-care v1.1 published 3 July 2026
supports: Monthly CC0 NWB geometry generates only two GM0928 border links, both parts of the same N300 physical corridor to Heerlen and Landgraaf. Nominal capacity 150 is a generalized scenario ceiling, and consecutive/paired evidence is not independent or additive throughput.

ProRail's CC0 register supplies Chevremont, Spekholzerheide, Eygelshoven Markt, Eygelshoven and Kerkrade Centrum; GTFS supplies 67 stop areas. Static geometry and schedules do not establish running trains/buses, accessible vehicles, passengers, evacuation/freight capacity, border continuation or restoration.

Two NDW/TrafficServiceTrack vehicle-obstruction records geometrically fall within GM0928, starting 1–2 September 2026 with unknown severity and no supplied end time. They are timestamped observations with source/validity metadata, not proof of closure extent, future persistence or the state of every road at a scenario checkpoint.

RIVM acute-care v1.1 assigns no acute-care point inside GM0928. Zuyderland states that its Heerlen emergency department provides 24/7 acute care; the RIVM questionnaire reports acute obstetrics, 24 treatment rooms and 38,500 visits in 2025. Register roles and annual counts do not establish incident-time acceptance, occupancy, staff, backup or route passability.

evidenceSources.publisher: Het Waterschapshuis / Stichting Mijn Aansluiting / Netbeheer Nederland / RDI / DUO / KNMI / RIVM
evidenceSources.title: E07 — Public water, provider, grid-planning, antenna, education, weather, seismic and air-quality context
evidenceSources.edition: Public-context snapshots retrieved 2–3 September 2026; provider records last updated 7 September 2025; contributor dates vary
supports: Full CBS-boundary containment assigns 20 HWH records to GM0928: six sewer pumps, RWZI Kaffeberg and 13 weirs. Every capacity is null; 13 name Waterschap Limburg and seven have null manager. IMWA/DAMO is CC BY-SA 4.0 with contributor-dependent completeness. Registration does not establish connected catchment, control, power/backup, operation or recovery.

The Public Domain Mijn Aansluiting point lookup identifies Enexis electricity/gas, WML drinking water and Ziggo media at the municipal reference point; drainage is empty. Provider records are dated 7 September 2025. Point responsibility is not municipal completeness, physical topology, current outage, water quality, capacity or restoration.

The single NBNL sample TERW Terwinselen reports withdrawal 156.9 MW existing, 116.8 MW required and 58 MW queued/120 requests; injection 151.3 MW existing, 118.4 MW required and 44.9 MW queued/51 requests; TenneT categories 3/3 and eleven projects, earliest 2028. It is periodically updated planning context with an unstated exact dataset licence, not live load, reserve or availability.

RDI WFS supplies 87 antenna records—45 mobile, 15 fixed link, 25 amateur, one broadcast and one other-mobile—and daily CC-BY DUO RIO supplies 15 education records. RDI's consumed service states no standard licence/cadence. Neither register proves coverage, backhaul, power, shelter role, occupancy, staff or supplies.

The bounded deployment assigns no Waterinfo observation/forecast, KNMI weather observation/warning, KNMI seismic origin or RIVM PM2.5 point inside GM0928. Each empty result is source/time/spatial NoData, not normal water/weather/air, zero seismic hazard or an all-clear.
